points.description: Asynchronous transmission sends each character as a self-contained unit surrounded by a start bit and a stop bit.
Synchronous transmission pools several characters into a continuous stream of data called a frame or block instead of sending each character independently.
Synchronous frames are delimited by a SYN character or a flag.
Asynchronous transmission is easy and cheap to implement but results in low transmission rates.
Synchronous transmission is more complex but achieves higher transmission rates.
Synchronous transmission requires synchronization between the sender and the receiver.
